literal_meaning: গলায় ধারণ করা (wearing around the neck)
figurative_meaning_bn: বৈষ্ণব বেশ তুলসীর মালা গলায় পরা
figurative_meaning_en: Adopting the guise of a Vaishnava by wearing a tulsi garland around the neck, implying superficial religious pretense
similar_in_english: wearing one's piety on one's sleeve
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে কণ্ঠিধারণ করে কিন্তু আসলে কোনো ভক্তি নেই।
এই সমাজে অনেকে কণ্ঠিধারণ করে প্রতারণা করে।
example_sentences_in_english: He does kanthidharan but has no real devotion.
In this society, many pretend piety through kanthidharan.
history: This idiom draws from Vaishnava traditions in Bengal, where wearing a tulsi mala symbolizes devotion to Lord Krishna, but here it critiques insincere adoption of such practices.
note: The idiom highlights cultural critique of religious hypocrisy in Bengali Hindu society.
